I am posting this to guns because their doesn't seem to be a place to post about non fire arm projectile weapons. Any way I have been thinking of a way to improve the range and accuracy of a crossbow. I mean a 35 yard max effective range shot from a cross bow is just not realistic. I can do that with my M1911 .45 ACP.

Most modern cross bows fire a 400 grain bolt at about 350-500 fps. The bolt will experience a 25 inch drop at 50 yards with a 400 fps launching velocity and a flight time of about 1/8 of a second.

The majority problems with a cross bow is the bolt. The bolt is inherently inaccurate because the size and weigh of the point at the front and the size and light weight of the fletches at the rear cause the bolt to slow down rapidly and the weight of the point vs air resistance and the light weight of the fletches and the air resistance causes the bolt to want to weather vane and point downward. The is why arrows when fired from long distances always land point down. Now some of this can be compensated from by making the point an airfoil. A NACA 65-206 to a NACA65-209 airfoil should provide enough lift yet not create excessive drag to keep the head flying parallel to the direction of travel. The fletching at the back should be a NACA 65-206 as there is not that much weight so it would not need to have the lift of the point. The two airfoils working in conjunction should keep the bolt parallel to the direction of flight and reduce the overall drag of the shaft as it would not be traveling at an angle to the direction of flight. This should go a long way to conserve the velocity and the energy of the bolt. If the point of the bolt were a quadrafoil point the vertical foils would act at vertical stabilizers and keep the bolt more stable in flight. With better aerodynamics and stabilization of the bolt the range and accuracy of the cross bow should improve dramatically. Consistent 100 yard effective shot should become possible.
I've got a crossbow myself. I'd love to see some more research and development of this idea.

Most of the energy of these types of projectiles is lost from harmonic oscillation and air resistance. In other words the bolt wiggles through the air as a consequence of the flex in the material responding to the compressive force the string exerts on the back of the bolt. If you can figure out a dampening mechanism inside the bolt there will be more energy in the system to convert to forward velocity.

As to the aerodynamics of the bolt, a cylindrical lifting body would be ideal. It should probably look something like a sharpened donut from the front profile or the front housing of a jet engine's covering shroud.
